newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products hold firm tone, markets tight.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products hold firm tone, markets tight.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to firm on Wednesday.
Gasoline prices held steady with transatlantic arbitrage options supportive and the spot market balanced as maintenance and poor reforming margins continue to cap refinery output.

Traders said recent sales into the Lebanon had also helped draw down lengthy low octane supplies although several East Med cargoes were still showing. Naphtha markets were steady with prompt offers scarce, but a 60 kt Algerian cargo was still being talked at around benchmark cif high quotes +$2/+3 a tonne.
Gas oil was firmer, with an Italian refiner reporting that a 0.2 percent heating oil cargo loading on Wednesday had traded at fob quotes high +$3.75 cif Italian islands.

Demand for inferior spec material was also seen into the Turkey, Syria and Lebanon, while shipping sources reported that Brazil's Petrobras had fixed a 73,000 cargo for October 20 to take 0.1 percent sulphur product from Sicily.
"They are locked into a term contract, but prices are so high want top ups for economies of scale," a trader said.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil markets were quiet but the tone was firm.
Little supply was seen and there was outstanding demand for two 300 cst Tunisian cargoes for the end of the month. Offers for this requirement were talked at around $6 over the quoted fob high.

Low sulphur markets were quiet and tight too. A French cargo was heard sold to a trader at $124.50 fob NWE. This was $1 below the level of Oct swaps, and the market is backwardated by around $1 a month.
Offers were seen into Italy on Tuesday at $129 cif Med but no offer numbers were heard on Wednesday.
